name: Cilnidipine
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Cilnidipine is a dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker (L- and N-type) metabolized by CYP3A4 with no unchanged drug in urine. In patients with serum creatinine 1.5 to 3.1 mg/dL its levels were the same as with normal kidney function, and the Japanese insert sets no kidney dose change. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: Japanese kidney data are by serum creatinine (1.5 to 3.1 mg/dL); bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl) by judgment.

bands.recommendation: Usual: 5 to 10 mg once daily after breakfast; up to 20 mg once daily (PMDA insert). Older adults: start 5 mg.

No kidney dose change in the Japanese insert. A 10 mg dose in patients with serum creatinine 1.5 to 3.1 mg/dL gave levels no different from normal kidney function, with no accumulation over 7 days (PMDA insert).

Not studied below the creatinine range tested (1.5 to 3.1 mg/dL). Hepatically cleared, so a change is not expected; titrate from 5 mg.

hd: Not studied in dialysis (PMDA insert). Hepatically cleared; start low and titrate.
monitoring: Blood pressure (avoid excessive lowering in older adults); liver tests if symptoms (hepatic dysfunction, jaundice); platelets (thrombocytopenia under 0.1%) (PMDA insert).
